screen: Production Notifications (phone 390, full page), Stage 5 pass 3

expected_differences: The supplied Lab capture is Profile, not Notifications. A flat utility list without the graphite identity masthead, vehicle assembly or work gallery is appropriate here.
The real business identity and five-item business navigation correctly replace Maya’s personal identity and navigation.
Notification titles, campaign names, handles, dates, payment amounts and existing [demo] text come from stored records; they should not be rewritten to resemble Lab fixtures.
The three unread records correctly produce three cobalt dots, a muted “3 new” count and the bell badge.
No source-to-commitment offset is needed for this text-based notification list; adding one would be decorative.
keep: Mineral canvas, flat rows, restrained dividers and white bottom navigation without card shadows.
Strong page heading, 16px phone gutters, readable wrapping and muted supporting text.
Needs review items before accepted-request and welcome notifications.
Stored titles preserved, with linked request context beneath bare titles and no duplicated campaign subtitle where the title already identifies it.
Unread emphasis through heavier ink titles and cobalt dots; the page count remains muted.
Conditional “approve to pay” wording for $75 and $25, without presenting either amount as earned or paid.
Business remains visibly current through its cobalt selection edge and bold label.
review.readiness_note: Sign off the visual transfer at 390px. The capture preserves the visible records, states, account controls and navigation; actual deep-link destinations, read-state persistence and control behavior still require interaction testing.
review.why: This is a faithful system-level transfer rather than a literal copy of the Profile reference. The mineral surface, ink/muted hierarchy, thin separators and restrained cobalt retain Frame Shift without imposing a discovery composition on management UI. Review items lead the list, long stored titles and source descriptions wrap without clipping, timestamps remain distinct, and conditional payment language stays attached to its notification. The three unread indicators agree with both counts. Search, Messages, Notifications, account switching and the business navigation remain exposed, with Business correctly selected. No blocking visual drift is evident at this viewport.
review.verdict: Yes—Frame Shift is faithfully applied to Notifications at 390px, with no visible loss of production functionality and no blocking design drift.
